Outline: Agents

01 · How an Agent Takes Actions

§ Reasoning and Actions

Recap: Retrieval and ToolsA retrieval pipeline fixes the search step before generation

Agents add tool use to the components seen so far

AgentAn agent uses a model to choose actions toward a task

The loop repeats until a stop rule fires

ReActReAct alternates reasoning, actions, and observations

An observation can change the next action

ReAct ExampleTool observations provide facts that the model can use

The answer depends on observations from external tools

Caveat: Unsupported ActionA model can request a tool that does not match the task

The runtime, not the model, decides what may run

Tool CallingThe model proposes a structured tool name and arguments

The model asks; the application executes

Tool DefinitionA typed LangChain tool executes one bounded read

const readPressure = tool(({pump_id}) => {
  const row = readings[pump_id];
  if (!row) throw Error("Unknown pump");
  return {pump_id, ...row};
}, {name:"read_pressure", description:"Read one pump pressure in bar",
  schema:z.object({pump_id:z.enum(["P-17","P-18"])})});
return await readPressure.invoke({pump_id:"P-17"});

§ Tool Execution

Tool ContractSpecify what a tool accepts, changes, and returns

Four facts every tool must declare

Model Context ProtocolMCP standardizes how applications connect to capability servers

One protocol between the host and every capability server

Caveat: MCP and PermissionA connected server may expose more capability than a task needs

Expose only the tools this task needs

Agent RuntimeThe runtime owns execution, validation, and state updates

Invalid actions return as errors, not executions

Bounded Agent LoopObserve a model decision, tool execution, and the next decision

const model = makeModel([
  '{"tool":"read_pressure","pump_id":"P-17"}',
  '{"final":"P-17 pressure is 4.2 bar; threshold 5 bar."}'
]);
const messages = [new HumanMessage("Check P-17 pressure. Return JSON tool or final.")];
const trace = [];
for (let step=0; step<3; step++) {
  const raw = await model.invoke(messages);
  const decision = await new JsonOutputParser().invoke(raw);
  trace.push({step,decision});
  if (decision.final) return {mode:MODEL_MODE, trace};
  if (decision.tool !== "read_pressure") throw Error("Unknown tool");
  const observation = await pressureTool.invoke({pump_id:decision.pump_id});
  trace.push({observation});
  messages.push(raw, new HumanMessage(JSON.stringify(observation)));
}
throw Error("Step budget exceeded");

Stopping RulesStop on completion, limits, or an unresolved failure

Four ways a loop ends; only one is success

02 · Controlling Workflows and State

§ Control Flow

Chain CompositionA chain fixes the order of prompt, model, and parsing stages

Fixed composition is suitable when the dependencies are known

Adaptive Control FlowAn agent may choose a different next step after observing a result

The observation changes which branch runs

Kinds of AgentsAgents differ in how much of the control flow the model decides

A router picks one branch; an autonomous agent picks every step

Control and ReliabilityGiving the model more control tends to lower application reliability

A developer-defined graph keeps model choices inside fixed structure

Controlled WorkflowDevelopers define parts of the control flow explicitly

Some steps follow a fixed path

LangGraphLangGraph represents stateful workflows with nodes and edges

Nodes update state; edges select the next node

Workflow GraphUse conditional edges to send stale readings to review

const State = Annotation.Root({pump_id:Annotation(), reading:Annotation(),
  outcome:Annotation()});
const graph = new StateGraph(State)
 .addNode("read", async s => ({reading:await pressureTool.invoke({pump_id:s.pump_id})}))
 .addNode("report", s => ({outcome:s.reading.pressure_bar > 5 ? "alarm" : "normal"}))
 .addNode("review", () => ({outcome:"stale; review required"}))
 .addEdge(START,"read")
 .addConditionalEdges("read", s => s.reading.age_minutes > 10 ? "review" : "report")
 .addEdge("report",END).addEdge("review",END)
 .compile();
const result = await graph.invoke({pump_id:"P-17"});
return {reading:result.reading, outcome:result.outcome};

§ State and Recovery

Agent StateState contains the information needed to continue the current run

The model sees a slice of the run state

Memory TypesDifferent retained information supports different decisions

TypeContainsExample
Working stateCurrent task progressA pending tool call
Semantic memoryStored factsPreferred report format
Episodic memoryPast events and outcomesA resolved maintenance case
Procedural memoryReusable instructionsA validated inspection procedure
Choose what to remember before choosing where to store it

Caveat: Stale MemoryA stored fact can outlive the condition that made it true

A remembered fact outlived the condition

CheckpointA checkpoint saves the state needed to resume a workflow

A checkpoint after each node limits repeated work

Caveat: Resume and Side EffectsResuming a workflow can repeat an external write

Resuming repeated a write

Approval BoundaryPause before a consequential action and resume with a recorded decision

The run waits for a recorded decision

Agent TraceTrace actions and observations instead of relying on the final narrative

The trace shows each node, state update and message

03 · Connecting Agents to Data

§ Text-to-SQL

Data AgentsHere, a data agent is an agent that reads and writes data systems

Reads and writes go through separate tools

Text-to-SQLText-to-SQL translates a natural-language question into a database query

Schema context turns a question into a checkable query

Recap: Factory TablesMachine 1 is P-17; each row in Runs records one production run

Keys and grain decide which joins are valid

Schema ContextExpose names, types, keys, and grain before generating SQL

The prompt carries keys, grain and the metric

Weighted YieldAggregate counts before dividing when run sizes differ

Sum the counts, then divide

Line Yield QueryJoin by the declared key and divide the aggregated counts

SELECT m.line, SUM(r.good) AS good, SUM(r.total) AS total,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(r.good) / NULLIF(SUM(r.total),0),2) AS yield_pct
FROM Runs r JOIN Machines m ON m.id=r.machine_id
GROUP BY m.line ORDER BY m.line;
The result uses production counts rather than an average of run ratios

Caveat: Join MultiplicationAn extra one-to-many join can inflate both counts and rankings

Three notes triple the production count

Query Validation LayersCheck syntax, access, resources, and semantics separately

A query that runs can still be wrong

Read-Only Query ToolExecute queries under a constrained database identity

Validated SQL → DB role → Budget → Result

Demo: Factory YieldRun the calculation in the local SQLite database

  1. Return total good and total output for each line
  2. Calculate weighted yield as a percentage
Ctrl/⌘ + Enter

Answer: Factory YieldLine A yields 83.75%; line B yields 95%

SELECT m.line, SUM(r.good) AS good, SUM(r.total) AS total,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(r.good)/NULLIF(SUM(r.total),0),2) AS yield_pct
FROM Runs r JOIN Machines m ON m.id=r.machine_id
GROUP BY m.line ORDER BY m.line;
The answer follows the stated metric and joins

Text-to-SQL ExecutionPass schema and metric meaning into the model, then execute the query

const prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.fromMessages([
 ["system", "Return JSON with sql. Only read Machines and Runs. " + DB_SCHEMA],
 ["human", "{question}"]
]);
const model = makeModel([JSON.stringify({sql:YIELD_SQL})]);
const proposed = await prompt.pipe(model).pipe(new JsonOutputParser())
 .invoke({question:"Yield by line over all runs?"});
const rows = await dbQuery(proposed.sql); // SQLite enforces query-only mode
return {mode:MODEL_MODE, sql:proposed.sql, rows};

§ Writes and Access

Case study: Repair Request WorkflowA repair task crosses query, permission, and write boundaries

StageContractEvidence
Find machineAuthorized lookupMachine ID + current state
Check readingsFreshness + unitsTimestamped measurements
Propose repairBounded write + reviewTarget + reason + request ID
Create requestTransaction + idempotencyStored row + receipt
The final answer follows verified reads and a confirmed write

Transaction BoundaryA transaction groups changes that must succeed or fail together

Both writes happen, or neither

Idempotent RequestA uniqueness constraint can prevent duplicate requests

CREATE TABLE Repairs (
  request_id TEXT UNIQUE,
  machine_id INTEGER,
  reason TEXT,
  status TEXT
);
-- The server also verifies that repeated IDs carry the same payload.

Caveat: Timeout After CommitA missing response does not reveal whether the write succeeded

The retry finds the committed request

Demo: Duplicate Repair RequestUse SQLite to observe a unique request key

  1. Insert req_42 twice in one execution using INSERT OR IGNORE
  2. Select Repairs and verify that one row remains
Ctrl/⌘ + Enter

Answer: Duplicate Repair RequestThe unique key leaves one record after two identical inserts

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Repairs VALUES ('req_42',1,'vibration','open');
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO Repairs VALUES ('req_42',1,'vibration','open');
SELECT * FROM Repairs;
This example demonstrates uniqueness, not the entire write policy

Role-Based Access ControlRBAC grants capabilities to roles assigned to authenticated identities

Identity → Role → Permission → Resource

Caveat: Prompt-Based AccessA prompt cannot replace a database permission check

Only the database permission stops the query

Row Filters and Column MasksFilter records and redact sensitive values at query time

Same table, different visibility per caller

Column Masking ExampleThe same row can expose different values to different roles

machine_idRoleemail visible
1Operator with approved accessoperator1@example.test
1Analyst[masked]
Masking changes visibility without changing the source record

Agent EvaluationTest the outcome, the action path, and the database state

DimensionCheck
Task successRequired result verified by evidence
Tool behaviorCorrect tool, arguments, and access scope
RecoveryTimeouts and duplicate requests handled
EfficiencyCalls, tokens, and elapsed time
An agent test observes both the final answer and the changed state

Takeaway: Bound actions, recover state, govern data

1Validate tool requests and bound the agent loop
2Keep workflow state outside the model so runs can pause and resume
3Connect agents to data through read-only queries, transactions, and roles
